name: rightsize
description: Make every Claude token count. rightsize sends each Claude Code prompt to the cheapest model and effort that does the job, raises effort only when Claude is actually stuck, and keeps your cache and context from costing more than they should: routine work stays on Sonnet or goes to a Haiku helper, reviews switch to Opus for one turn, and it learns from your own outcomes which routes to trust. No profiles, no tuning. A band shows what it did and what it cost, and watch-only mode lets you see its calls before it changes anything.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: act (default): rightsize changes effort, switches reviews to Opus and hands work to helpers as your rules say. watch only: it rates and plans every prompt, applies nothing, and the band says what it would have done; /rightsize report sums what that would have saved. Use it for a week to see rightsize's calls on your own work before turning it on.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: on (default): rightsize changes effort on your main chat (lowering for easy prompts, raising for hard ones, a session switch you pick), runs a review on Opus for one turn, and raises effort mid-turn when Claude looks stuck, as your rules say. off: none of those happen; your effort and model stay as you set them. With Routing and Hand-offs both off, rightsize rates no prompt and spends nothing on rating (the cache features still work). A row below that belongs to Routing, such as Raise when stuck, is then not used.

handOffs.title: Hand-offs
handOffs.description: on (default): rightsize hands work to a helper subagent (a cheaper model for routine work, a stronger one for hard work) that your main chat briefs and checks, and runs Claude's own subagents on the cheapest model that fits. off: no hand-offs, and Claude's subagents stay on their model; when Routing is on, an effort change replaces the hand-off. With Routing and Hand-offs both off, rightsize rates no prompt and spends nothing on rating (the cache features still work).

askFirst.title: Ask before changing
askFirst.description: off (default): rightsize lowers or raises effort, switches a review to Opus and hands work to a helper without asking, and the band says what it did. on: every move rightsize would make on its own asks first, in a timed dialog (see Question wait), and nothing changes until you answer. Either way an Advanced rule row you set (Lowering, Raising, Stronger model, Cheaper model) wins for its case. A Quality profile saved by an older release reads as on until you set this row.

cache.title: Cache
cache.description: on (default): rightsize keeps an eye on the prompt cache: the offer to keep it warm, keep warm itself, a handoff or a compaction before it goes cold, and the idle warning when you return to a cold cache. off: none of those; a keep-warm run in progress stops at once. The rows Idle warning and Before the cache goes cold fine-tune it while Cache is on, and are not used while it is off.

band.title: Band
band.description: The row above the prompt that shows what rightsize did, with buttons to retry it at the original effort or run it on your model, and a ⋯ menu to change the rule, mark a hand-off or lowering 👍 or 👎 (kept on this machine), or change cache choices. when it acts: only when it changes something. always: on every rated prompt, no change included. off: status line only.

floor.title: Advanced · Lowest effort
floor.description: The lowest effort level rightsize will lower to.

ceiling.title: Advanced · Highest effort
ceiling.description: The highest effort level rightsize will raise to. It never goes above this: not when a prompt needs more, not mid-turn when Claude looks stuck (those also never reach max), and not for the subagent it hands work to, which runs at most at this level. A level you are already on above it is left alone: this stops raises, it never lowers.

lowerRule.title: Advanced · Lowering
lowerRule.description: When a prompt needs less effort. ask me: ask each time. lower automatically: lower without asking. never lower: never. not set (the default): Ask before changing decides (off: done without asking; on: asked first), and the band says so the first time the case comes up in a session, with the other rules in its ⋯ menu. A rule set here is used as it is. The band's ⋯ menu and /rightsize settings set it too; set it back to not set to let Ask before changing decide again.

raiseRule.title: Advanced · Raising
raiseRule.description: When a prompt needs more effort on the same model. ask me: ask each time. raise automatically: raise without asking. never raise: never. While Raise when stuck is follow Raising, this rule also decides raises mid-turn when Claude looks stuck. not set (the default): Ask before changing decides (off: done without asking; on: asked first), and the band says so the first time the case comes up in a session, with the other rules in its ⋯ menu. A rule set here is used as it is. The band's ⋯ menu and /rightsize settings set it too; set it back to not set to let Ask before changing decide again.

upRule.title: Advanced · Stronger model
upRule.description: When a stronger model than yours would do better, or a review runs on Opus for one turn. ask first: ask before it. always send: do it without asking. stay, raise effort only: stay on your model and raise effort. ask each time: ask what to do each time. not set (the default): Ask before changing decides (off: done without asking; on: asked first), and the band says so the first time the case comes up in a session, with the other rules in its ⋯ menu. A rule set here is used as it is. The band's ⋯ menu and /rightsize settings set it too; set it back to not set to let Ask before changing decide again.

downRule.title: Advanced · Cheaper model
downRule.description: When a task could run on a cheaper model than yours. ask first: ask before sending it to a subagent on that model. always send: send it without asking. stay, lower effort only: stay on your model and lower effort. ask each time: ask what to do each time. not set (the default): Ask before changing decides (off: done without asking; on: asked first), and the band says so the first time the case comes up in a session, with the other rules in its ⋯ menu. A rule set here is used as it is. The band's ⋯ menu and /rightsize settings set it too; set it back to not set to let Ask before changing decide again.

useHaiku.title: Advanced · Use Haiku
useHaiku.description: on: rightsize may hand work to Haiku, and move Claude's own subagents to it. off: it never does, and the starting-point comparison leaves Haiku out. Haiku still rates your prompts (it is the rater, not a worker), so this does not stop the rating calls.

useFable.title: Advanced · Use Fable
useFable.description: on: rightsize may hand work to Fable when the work needs a stronger model. off: it never does, and the starting-point comparison leaves Fable out. If you work on Fable yourself, nothing changes.

subagents.title: Advanced · Claude's subagents
subagents.description: cheaper when it fits: when Claude starts a general-purpose subagent without naming a model, rate its brief and run it on the cheapest weaker model that fits, at that model's level, under the 70% hand-off bar. off: leave Claude's own subagents on its model.

workflows.title: Advanced · Workflows
workflows.description: What rightsize does once Claude starts a workflow (ultracode, or asked for): many helper agents at once, often 10 or more, each picking its own model. ask: ask on the band when the first workflow starts (the default); until you answer, rightsize pauses for it. pause rightsize: hand nothing off for the rest of the session, and leave the workflow's agents alone. follow my rules: hand-offs follow your Stronger model and Cheaper model rules as usual; the workflow's agents are left alone. right-size every agent: as follow my rules, and each workflow agent that names no model is rated by the Rater (one rating call each) and runs on the cheapest model that fits, under Claude's subagents, Use Haiku, Use Fable and the miss-rate pause (20%). Claude's subagents set to off keeps the agents alone in every case. Whichever you pick, measurement stays paused after a workflow: calibration learns nothing and no saving is claimed.

pacing.title: Advanced · Budget pacing
pacing.description: on: on a subscription, move the hand-off and lowering bars by how fast the 5-hour and 7-day windows are being used. Running out early: hand off and lower more readily, and the band says which bars moved. Much left near a reset: nothing changes. Over 90% used: save all it can, which skips raises and stronger models while Raising and Stronger model are not set. A rule you set stays as you set it. off: always use the fixed bars (70% for hand-offs, 90% for lowering).

escalation.title: Advanced · Raise when stuck
escalation.description: What to do when a turn shows Claude is stuck (the same tool call failing twice, 3 tool calls failing, the same call running 3 times, a turn passing 3x the rated steps (at least 15) with no progress, or 2 fixes in a row leaving the tests red). A raise is one level for the rest of the turn, at most twice, never above Highest effort and never to max. follow Raising (the default): the Raising rule decides. ask me: ask on the band while the turn goes on. raise automatically: raise without asking, whatever Raising says. off: never raise mid-turn. The same rule covers a helper that looks stuck. The question's "for this session" answer lasts until the session ends; "Always raise when stuck" sets this row to raise automatically. A value of on from an older release reads as follow Raising.

startTips.title: Advanced · Start suggestions
startTips.description: weekly or monthly: every 7 or 30 days, estimate what the last 30 days of rated prompts would have cost from Sonnet and Opus at medium and high, rightsize's changes counted. Prompts Haiku's rating has often got wrong for a model count against that model's start. When another start is at least 15% cheaper (25% while it has few measured runs) without sending over 1 prompt in 10 to a stronger model, or when over 15% of prompts needed a stronger model or more effort, the band suggests switching with /model. rightsize never changes your model itself. off: no suggestions; /rightsize report still shows the comparison.

idleWarning.title: Advanced · Idle warning
idleWarning.description: When a session sat idle past the cache's life (1 hour, or 5 minutes when prices.json says 5m), the next prompt writes the whole conversation to the cache again. When that costs over this much more than a warm cache, the band notes the cost beside what rightsize did with the prompt (as a share of the 5-hour window on a subscription, once runs show the rate), and what /compact first would have cost. The prompt is never held. The same amount is the size bar for Before the cache goes cold.

beforeCold.title: Advanced · Before the cache goes cold
beforeCold.description: What rightsize does when a session that ends a turn with a big conversation (a cold return would cost at least the Idle warning amount, $0.50 by default and while Idle warning is off, API-equivalent on a subscription) is about to lose its prompt cache. keep warm 2 h, keep warm 8 h, keep warm until my usual start (the time you usually send your first prompt, at most 8 hours): send one tiny request just before each expiry to keep the cache warm until then, with a status row on the band (Stop keeping warm; Don't keep warm again in ⋯), and stop when you type, press Stop, a request fails, or keeping warm would cost more than coming back cold. ask: offer the choices on the band 5 minutes after the turn, each with its cost, and do nothing if you do not pick. save a handoff: run whatsnext's wrap-up once before expiry (compact when whatsnext is not installed or not started in the project). compact: compact once before expiry (with whatsnext, using its instructions). off: nothing. Nothing runs during a turn. Not set here, rightsize keeps warm until your usual start.
options: keep warm until my usual start

billing.title: Advanced · Reports
billing.description: api: subagent reports show dollars. subscription: they show the share of usage and of the 5-hour window, with API-equivalent dollars beside it. rightsize reads this off each response's rate limits when they show it. A value set here is your answer: the rate limits never change it, and /rightsize says when they disagree.

longHelpers.title: Advanced · Long helpers
longHelpers.description: What happens when a helper on a cheaper model nears its spend limit (a multiple of the main-model estimate for its task) and is still finding new things. ask: ask on the band whether to let it continue; no answer means it stops at the limit and reports. continue while making progress: extend its limit automatically, one block at a time, up to 10x the estimate, then ask. stop at the limit: never extend. A helper that is stuck is stopped with no question.

outputAdvice.title: Advanced · Output suggestion
outputAdvice.description: on: once a session, when output is a large share of the cost (at least 25%, after 20 requests and $1.00 spent at list prices), suggest the Concise output style. off: never suggest it. This row does not change your output style. To use Concise in every project, set Output style to Concise in your Claude settings.
